# Results — Study 389 (Name-Change-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore — a company that
**rebrands toward the hot theme** (`.com`, `Blockchain`, `AI`) **pops** on the rename and
then **gives it all back** — tested as a small **event study** over a hardcoded, transparent
table of ~25 real theme-chasing rebrands across the three waves. Around each rename we
measure the abnormal (excess-of-SPY) return on a short **pop** leg `[+1…+5d]` and a longer
**fade** leg `[+6…+65d]`, with a 1-day entry lag. Offline & deterministic for the synthetic
control; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY + ~25 rebrand tickers (public, no key) |
| Window | 1995-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (cached); event windows fall within it |
| Rebrand table | **25** documented theme-chasing renames; **8** famous ones DELISTED (named) |
| Events priced | **21** of 25 (rest delisted, listed after the announce, or window overran) |
| Pop / fade legs | abnormal excess-of-SPY return over `[+1…+5d]` (pop) and `[+6…+65d]` (fade) |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; small-cap one-way 30 bps × 4 crossings on the believers' trade |

> **Survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The loudest give-backs — **Long
> Island Iced Tea → Long Blockchain** (~+200–300% then delisted), **UBI Blockchain
> Internet**, **KodakCoin**, several dot-com renames — **delisted** and leave **no**
> yfinance series. The priced sample is therefore the set of rebrands that *survived*, biased
> **toward** names that did not collapse and **against** the believers' fade. A survivor-only
> fade that comes out *positive* is thus a **conservative** refutation of "give it back."

## The signal — abnormal returns on each leg vs zero

1-day entry lag. The Welch *t* tests each leg's cross-sectional mean against zero; the
placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size non-event windows (same tickers) whose
mean abnormal return matches/beats the rebrand set in magnitude.

| leg | n | mean abnormal | win-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **pop** `[+1…+5d]`   | 21 | **+1.24%** | 52% | **+0.51** | 0.496 |
| **fade** `[+6…+65d]` | 21 | **+16.22%** | 52% | **+1.16** | 0.089 |

Read it carefully. The **pop** is a faint **+1.2%** abnormal return over the first week —
positive, but a coin-flip win-rate (52%) and **t = 0.51**: indistinguishable from no pop at
all. The **fade** is the punchline: on the survivor tape it is **+16%** — *positive*, the
**opposite** of "give it back." Survivors who renamed toward the theme kept drifting **up**
over the next three months (and even that is not significant, t = 1.16, placebo p = 0.09).
The two-legged story needs a significant **+pop** and a significant **−fade**; the tape
delivers an insignificant small pop and an insignificant *positive* fade. Neither leg of the
legend is real here.

## By wave — the give-back is nowhere

| wave | n | mean pop | mean fade |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| dot-com (1999–2000) | 7 | −1.31% | −3.09% |
| blockchain (2017–2020) | 6 | +1.93% | **+61.95%** |
| AI (2020–2024) | 8 | +2.96% | −1.18% |

The dot-com survivors barely moved (the spectacular renames delisted — survivorship). The
blockchain survivors **mooned** (RIOT, BTBT, MSTR rode the 2020–21 crypto bull *up* +62% over
the fade window — the reverse of a give-back). The AI survivors popped a little and went
roughly flat. There is no wave in which the surviving rebrands "gave it back."

## The believers' trade loses money gross — before costs even bite

The folklore trade is: **buy the pop, then flip short to capture the fade.** Per event that is
`pop − fade` (long the pop, short the fade).

| | per-event P&L |
|---|--:|
| gross combo (long pop, short fade) | **−14.98%** |
| net @ 30 bps/leg × 4 crossings | **−16.18%** |

Because the fade is *positive*, shorting it **loses** — the combo is **−15% gross**, and four
small-cap crossings at 30 bps make it **−16% net**. There is nothing to harvest: the trade
the legend prescribes is a money-loser on the real tape before costs, and worse after.

## Robustness — the result is flat in the window choice

| pop / fade days | n | pop mean | pop *t* | fade mean | fade *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 / 40   | 21 | −1.48% | −0.46 | +16.19% | +1.32 |
| **5 / 60** | 21 | +1.24% | +0.51 | +16.22% | +1.16 |
| 10 / 120 | 21 | +1.09% | +0.29 | +51.68% | +1.36 |

No window makes the pop significant, and the fade is **positive at every horizon** (never the
negative give-back the story needs). The verdict does not hinge on the exact window.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and ~25 events are weak

On deterministic event windows where we *plant* a known pop + give-back of size `edge`:

| planted edge | n | pop mean | pop *t* | fade mean | fade *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 25 | +2.22% | +1.52 | +5.64% | +1.19 |
| **+0.40** (huge pop+dump) | 25 | +52.50% | +24.05 | −29.19% | −9.21 |

With **no** planted edge neither leg clears *t* = 2 (it cannot manufacture significance from
~25 noisy events). Only a **huge** planted +40% pop-then-full-give-back lights up both legs —
and there the fade comes out correctly **negative** (*t* = −9.2), exactly the give-back the
real tape lacks. The control proves the measurement engine is unbiased **and** that a
couple-dozen events can only detect an implausibly large effect — exactly why a survivor table
of ~21 rebrands cannot certify the legend.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The dot-com academic anchor (Cooper-Dimitrov-Rau 2001) makes the *pop*
  real in 1998–99, but on this ~21-event survivor tape the pop is **+1.2%** at **t = 0.51**
  (placebo p = 0.50) — a positive whisper inside its own error bar — and the **fade is
  *positive* (+16%, t = 1.16)**, not the negative give-back the story needs. Literature
  support + an insignificant, sign-wrong point estimate ⇒ **WEAK**, not REAL. Survivorship is
  named on this axis: the worst give-backs delisted, so the surviving fade is biased *up*.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The believers' buy-the-pop / short-the-fade trade is **−15%
  gross** per event (you lose shorting a fade that doesn't happen) and **−16% net** of four
  small-cap crossings. There is no edge to harvest, at any size.
- **Pop then dump? — BUSTED.** The legend is a **selection-on-anecdotes** illusion: Long
  Blockchain and KodakCoin are remembered *because* they were extreme, and they **delisted**,
  so they never enter a survivor table. Across a representative sample of surviving rebrands
  the pop is a coin-flip and the "give-back" runs the wrong way. The romantic pop-and-dump is
  real-as-anecdote, absent-as-law.
